To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) 4-alkenyl- and 4-alkynyl-l-proline are not the direct precursors of the 4-alkyldihydroproline (APD) moieties of natural pyrrolobenzo-diazepines (natural PBDs), and 2) 4-ethylideneproline or 4-propylideneproline are the direct precursors for the APD moities of natural PBD,
the APD moeities of PBDs arise from a uniform building block that is modified postcondensation.
4-alkyldienyl-l-proline moieties of pyrrolobenozodiazepines are formed from 4-alkenyl-l-proline precursors via a FAD-dependent enzyme-catalyzed oxidation step.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the biosynthesis of the anticancer pyrrolo-benzodiazepine (PBD) antibiotics, which are characterized by a high degree of structural diversity.
the elucidation of the biosynthetic pathway leading to the formation of the 4-alkenyl-l-proline (AP) moiety of the pyrrolobenzo-diazepine (PBD) antitumor agents.
the biosynthesis and the structural diversity of the 4-alkyldihydroxyproline (APD) moiety of pyrrolobenzo[d]azepines (PDBs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PBD biosynthesis is not as simple as it has been assumed.

the PBDs are produced by a complex biosynthetic pathway, which includes the formation of the PBD ring system and the subsequent postcondensation modifications of the 4-alkenyl-l-proline building block.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biosynthetic machinery for pyrrolobenzo-diazepine (PBD) natural products has been elucidated in a step-by-step fashion.
APDs are the most diverse group of natural products that have ever been described in terms of the structural diversity of their alkyl side chain.
we have identified the building blocks for the APD moities and the enzymes involved in their postcondensation modification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthesis of PBDs is not as complex as was previously thought.
the structural diversity of APD moities of pyrrolobenzo- diazepines arises from postcondensation modifications of a uniform building block.
